articles.title: Bangalore Deep-Tech Growth Faces an Infrastructure Test - Urban Acres
articles.content: Home Analysis Bangalore’s Deep-Tech Rise Faces an Urban Infrastructure Test Analysis Bangalore’s Deep-Tech Rise Faces an Urban Infrastructure Test By Tenzin Choden November 24, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp Bangalore’s deep-tech ambitions are expanding across satellites, defence systems, semiconductor design and artificial intelligence, but the city’s ability to support that growth may depend on whether it can address long-standing failures in transport, utilities and basic urban infrastructure. A report carried by Hindustan Times and attributed to The Economist describes Bangalore as the centre of India’s emerging deep-tech economy. The city is reported to have more than 1,300 deep-tech companies, while funding for deep-tech startups across India is growing at almost twice the rate of funding for other startups, according to Nasscom-Zinnov. The report presents the shift as a new phase in Bangalore’s economic development. The city previously became the centre of India’s software and information-technology industry, supported by companies such as Infosys, Wipro and TCS. It later produced consumer-focused startups including Flipkart and Ola. The current expansion is centred on businesses involving advanced engineering and scientific research, including space, defence, semiconductors and artificial intelligence. The space sector illustrates the scale of the change. Pixxel, a Bangalore-based company, has raised $200 million, according to its founder Awais Ahmed, and has six satellites in orbit. Its satellites collect hyperspectral data that can be used to identify stressed crops, oil leakages and mineral deposits, as well as for military applications. The company hopes to increase its satellite fleet fourfold within a year, the report says. Other companies are also building capabilities in strategic sectors. Skyroot has become India’s first space unicorn, with a valuation of $1.1 billion, and has completed its first satellite launch, according to the report. Defence startups in Bangalore are developing solar-powered drones and radar systems, while Indian chip designers are establishing companies focused on power management and advanced computing. Sarvam, an Indian government-backed artificial-intelligence initiative, is reported to have reached a valuation of more than $1.5 billion after a $234 million funding round in June. This growth has been supported by a more active role for the Union government. The report says India opened its space sector to private enterprise in 2020 and created IN-SPACe to support private participation. It also refers to an $11 billion fund for high-risk research, disbursed through venture-capital funds, with the first awards made in October. Government assistance with security clearances and sensitive contracts has also helped some companies. That policy support creates a direct connection between national industrial strategy and city-level infrastructure. Bangalore attracts engineering graduates, global capability centres and founders working in highly specialised sectors. However, companies still depend on reliable roads, public transport, electricity, water, telecommunications and access to workplaces. Long commutes and unreliable civic services can increase operating costs and make it harder for the city to retain employees and attract new investment. The report identifies Bangalore’s urban governance as a serious concern, citing traffic congestion, unreliable utilities and broken pavements. It also describes a crater-sized pothole...

articles.title: NIELIT inaugurates temporary quantum- AI campus at Acharya Nagarjuna University
articles.content: Home NIELIT inaugurates temporary quantum-AI campus at Acharya Nagarjuna University NIELIT inaugurates temporary quantum-AI campus at Acharya Nagarjuna University A temporary campus described as India’s first dedicated quantum-AI university campus was inaugurated at Acharya Nagarjuna University in Guntur, Andhra Pradesh . It will operate from the university’s Centre for Distance Education building until the permanent campus is ready. The National Institute of Electronics and Information Technology (NIELIT) will offer training in quantum computing, artificial intelligence , chip design and semiconductors. Programmes are scheduled to begin on 1 December 2026. Four laboratories covering quantum computing, quantum communication, chip design and VLSI, and AI and computing are planned, with an investment of ₹47 crore. A permanent NIELIT campus is planned on 8.5 acres at Nidamarru in Amaravati. An investment of ₹730.70 crore has been approved for the project, and the Andhra Pradesh government has allocated the land. The project targets training about 8,250 people over five years through degree, skill-development and certification programmes. Notable Points Quantum algorithms: Peter Shor developed polynomial-time quantum algorithms for integer factorisation and the discrete logarithm problem in 1994. Lov Grover’s algorithm established a quantum speed-up for unstructured search in 1996. Quantum annealing: Quantum annealing can represent combinatorial optimisation problems as Ising models or quadratic unconstrained binary optimisation (QUBO) problems. Quantum computing: parallelism and limits: A superposition can encode outputs for several inputs, but measurement returns only one value, so parallelism alone does not ensure a speed-up. Quantum computing may improve the efficiency of some calculations, but it does not make undecidable problems such as the halting problem computable. articles.title: Varanasi Airport's 450-Metre Tunnel Beneath Runway Set to Complete by March 2027
articles.content: Nov 24, 2026 | Updated 02:15 PM GMT+5:30 Save & read from anywhere! Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app . Construction of the road underpass beneath the operational runway at Varanasi's Lal Bahadur Shastri International Airport has reached 60 per cent completion, with the project scheduled to be finished by March 2027. The 2.89 km underpass is being constructed along the Varanasi-Lucknow highway (NH-56) at an estimated cost of Rs 649.44 crore. TOI reported that during an inspection of the site, Divisional Commissioner K Vijayendra Pandian directed officials from the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) and the construction agency to accelerate work and ensure the project meets its deadline. The commissioner reviewed the construction progress and sought details of the challenges affecting execution. He stressed the need for regular monitoring, coordination between agencies and timely resolution of bottlenecks to prevent delays. The tunnel project, being executed in a modified form to account for technical challenges including groundwater levels. Once operational, all surface-level traffic near the runway will be eliminated, creating a safer airside environment whilst dramatically improving road connectivity through the 2.89 km highway realignment. The expanded runway will enable the airport to accommodate Code E wide-body aircraft, including the Boeing 777. The broader airport expansion will increase passenger capacity from 3.9 million to 9.9 million annually, with a new 75,000-square-metre terminal building and upgraded Category III Instrument Landing System. Construction work proceeds during night hours between 23:30 and 06:00, allowing daytime flight operations to continue uninterrupted. articles.title: New marine worm discovered in the Bay of Bengal marks India's first Hypereteone discovery ...
articles.content: General New marine worm discovered in the Bay of Bengal marks India’s first Hypereteone discovery in over nine decades A team of researchers from the Zoological Survey of India (ZSI), the Federal University of Maranhão in Brazil, and West Bengal State University has officially described a new species of marine worm, ... By Research Matters Staff Writer(s) · November 24, 2026 · Bay of Bengal · 4 min read EN Listen Add Research Matters as a Preferred Source on Google Hypereteone indica (credits - authors of the study https://doi.org/10.1080/17451000.2026.2724895) Credit: Authors of the study A team of researchers from the Zoological Survey of India (ZSI), the Federal University of Maranhão in Brazil, and West Bengal State University has officially described a new species of marine worm, named Hypereteone indica . The discovery represents the first new species of the genus Hypereteone identified in Indian waters in more than ninety years, since the description of Hypereteone barantollae in 1932. The new polychaete species was discovered along the sandy intertidal flats of the northern Bay of Bengal in eastern India, specifically across Udaypur beach in the Balasore district of Odisha and Hijli beach in the Purba Medinipur district of West Bengal. The specimens were collected during early morning low tides in September and December 2025. Because these worms vanish beneath the substrate immediately after sunrise, indicating marked light sensitivity and nocturnal or diel activity patterns, researchers had to track them and move quickly. They spotted and sampled live worms as they left distinctive mucus trails on the wet intertidal sand. They used fine 1 mm brushes, hand shovels, and worm-picking hooks to collect the samples. The specimens were carefully preserved and examined through compound light microscopy and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) at the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Kharagpur. The specific epithet indica is a Latin adjective meaning "from India," chosen to honour the country where the marine worm was discovered. Morphologically, Hypereteone indica belongs to the phyllodocid subfamily Eteoninae, commonly known as worker or trail worms due to their mucus-producing, sediment-burrowing habits. The new species is clearly differentiated from all nine other globally recognised Hypereteone species by a suite of distinct diagnostic features: its fully everted proboscis features exactly 14 rounded, globular terminal ring papillae, a bulbous proximal one-third adorned with transverse bands of minute tubercles, and a funnel-shaped distal region bearing six distinct longitudinal rugose ridges. Its compound chaetae possess an asymmetrical rostrum with a single large, blunt conical tooth, a consistently prominent primary tier tooth, and 4 to 5 tiers of smaller denticles. Unlike the sympatric H. barantollae , which possesses a broader prostomium, only five proboscideal ridges, and notably short ventral cirri, H. indica exhibits a prostomium that is about as long as wide, dorsal cirri that expand posteriorly, and ventral cirri that remain equal to or slightly longer than the neuropodia across body segments. articles.title: India's First Indigenous H5N1 Avian Influenza Vaccine | Indian Council of Agricultural Research
articles.content: A Major Breakthrough in Poultry Health The Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), through its National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases (ICAR-NIHSAD), Bhopal, has achieved a major breakthrough with the development of India’s first indigenous inactivated vaccine against Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI), commonly known as bird flu. Designed for chickens, the vaccine specifically targets H5N1 Clade 2.3.2.1a, responsible for most bird flu outbreaks in chickens. It is the world’s first vaccine developed against this specific variant, for which no specific commercial vaccine was previously available. The vaccine aims to protect against strains circulating in India and strengthen preparedness for controlling outbreaks. HPAI is a highly infectious disease that can cause mortality of nearly 100% among infected birds, leading to substantial losses through culling, movement restrictions and trade disruptions. Since its first detection in India in 2006, more than 500 combined outbreaks involving H5N1 and H5N8 subtypes have been reported. Its zoonotic potential also makes it a public health concern. The vaccine assumes significance given the scale of economic and livelihood risks associated with the disease. A major outbreak could put over 20% of India’s poultry population at risk and potentially reduce GDP growth by up to 1.5%. The 2006 outbreak alone caused estimated direct and indirect losses of ₹2,200–3,000 crore. By strengthening preventive disease control, the vaccine is expected to safeguard poultry health, reduce economic losses and protect farmers’ livelihoods. This breakthrough strengthens India’s indigenous animal vaccine development capabilities, poultry disease preparedness and biosecurity, while advancing the vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat and the integrated One Health approach, recognising the interconnectedness of animal, human and environmental health.

articles.title: Pune-based olee. space secures a DRDO contract for India's first laser-link drone ...
articles.content: Home Trending News Pune-based olee.space secures a DRDO contract for India’s first laser-link drone communication system Pune-based olee.space secures a DRDO contract for India’s first laser-link drone communication system Pune-based deep-tech company olee.space has secured a contract from the Defence Ministry's research and development arm, DRDO, to develop a laser-link drone communication system. By Ishita Ganguly 24 Nov 2026 00:45 IST Follow Us New Update olee.space gets DRDO contract Pune-based deep-tech company Olee Space has secured a contract from the Defence Ministry's research and development arm DRDO to develop a laser-link drone communication system. olee.space gets DRDO contract for laser-based drone communication system Under the contract, the startup will indigenously design and develop complete ground-based and airborne FSOC (free space optical communication) terminals equipped with automatic Pointing, Acquisition and Tracking (PAT) capabilities within 18 months, it said. The system will carry secure, high-speed, two-way data between ground stations and drones in flight, pairing a tripod-mounted ground terminal with a compact optical payload integrated into a drone, providing a high-bandwidth, full-duplex link over long line-of-sight ranges. Advertisment Add Startup Pedia As A Trusted Source In the Russia-Ukraine war, radio jamming became so effective that drones started flying with kilometres of fibre-optic cable trailing behind them to maintain connectivity, according to Olee Space. Though cables cannot be jammed, but they limit range and can snag or break, it further said. Laser links offer the same advantage without the tether, the startup said. It added that data travels on a narrow beam of light through open air. This produces fibre-like speed, impossible to intercept, and no vulnerability to radio jamming, according to olee.space. "Holding a laser link on a moving drone is one of the hardest problems in communications, and olee.space is one of very few companies globally working on this capability. We launched this programme a year ago. This is Aatmanirbhar Bharat in action: frontier technology, built in India, competing with the world," said James, Co-founder, olee.space. The Pune-based startup was founded in 2023 by IIT Bombay alumnus James Solomon and engineer Suman Hiremath. Its early research and development journey dates back to 2017, when Solomon began exploring laser-based communication technologies while working on defence-related projects. Olee Space specialises in Free-Space Optical Communication (FSOC), which uses infrared laser beams instead of conventional radio-frequency signals to transmit data at high speeds across land, air and space. The company is also developing quantum-secure communication systems and directed energy weapon technologies for defence applications, including counter-drone capabilities. Operating under the legal entity Citoto Digital Personality Private Limited, the company was incorporated in 2020, while its Olee Space venture is identified as having been founded in 2023. In August 2025, it raised $3 million in seed funding led by Rockstud Capital, with participation from other investors. The funding is intended to scale manufacturing, strengthen its communication technologies and advance its defence systems. articles.title: India's first bullet train to undergo trials in May 2027, Railway Minister announces
articles.content: India's first bullet train is expected to begin trial runs in May 2027 on a 50-km section between Surat and Bilimora, with electrification completed and signalling work targeted for January. Updated : Nov 24, 2026, 07:21 AM IST ndia's first bullet train project is moving towards its testing phase, with the initial trials expected to begin in May 2027 on the 50-km Surat-Bilimora stretch of the Mumbai-Ahmedabad high-speed rail corridor. Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw announced the timeline during a media briefing on Monday. He said electrification work on the section had been completed, while signalling-related work was expected to be finished by January 2027. Electrification completed on both tracks The overhead electrification system on the elevated Surat-Bilimora section was energised on November 20. The work covers both tracks and uses a 2x25 kV traction system. Installation work at the Bilimora traction substation has also been completed, marking an important step towards preparing the stretch for high-speed train operations. Vaishnaw said the entire Mumbai-Ahmedabad corridor would not become operational at once. Instead, the project would be opened in phases. B-28 train to be used for initial testing The initial trials will use the B-28 train, which is designed to run at speeds of up to 280 kmph. Vaishnaw explained that operating trains at speeds above 240 kmph requires specialised engineering. At such speeds, pressure forces generated by a moving train must be considered while designing both the coaches and the supporting infrastructure. He said the B-28 train had successfully completed a squeeze test. During the exercise, it was exposed to pressure levels twice the atmospheric pressure expected during actual operations. The test was conducted to assess how well the train could withstand pressure-related challenges during high-speed movement. Bullet train corridor to open in phases The proposed schedule sets different targets for various sections of the high-speed rail corridor. The Ahmedabad-Vapi stretch is expected to be completed by the end of 2027. The service is then targeted to reach Thane by 2029. The phased approach will allow different sections of the corridor to be completed and prepared for operations over time. Vaishnaw reviews construction progress in Maharashtra The Railway Minister also spoke about construction work in Maharashtra, including the undersea tunnel being built as part of the project. He expressed satisfaction with the progress made on these sections and described the construction activities as encouraging. The Mumbai-Ahmedabad high-speed rail corridor is India's first bullet train project. It is being developed to connect the two cities through a dedicated high-speed railway network.

articles.title: Ashok Leyland Flags Off India's First Blast-Protected Armoured Troop Transporters for CRPF ...
articles.content: Taking a massive leap forward in ensuring the safety of Indian security personnel, Ashok Leyland officially rolled out the country's first completely indigenous bullet- and blast-resistant Armoured Troop Transporter (ATT) on November 18. Built on a robust 4x4 platform, this 28-seater fortress on wheels is engineered to securely navigate high-risk combat zones. The development of this advanced vehicle directly addresses the tactical vulnerabilities exposed during the tragic February 2019 Pulwama terror attack, where a convoy ambush claimed the lives of 40 brave CRPF soldiers. Over the past seven years, Ashok Leyland collaborated closely with the armed forces to create a secure alternative to the unarmoured, soft-skinned buses traditionally used for moving troops through hostile territories. To modernise the frontline fleet, the Ministry of Home Affairs awarded a ₹187.24 crore contract to produce 124 units of these specialised vehicles. Under this initial order, the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) will receive the lion's share with 109 units, while the Border Security Force (BSF) will induct the remaining 15. Destined for counter-insurgency and counter-terrorism operations in volatile regions like Jammu and Kashmir, the Central Motor Vehicles Rules (CMVR)-certified transporter brings uncompromised protection to convoy movements. The heavily armoured shell provides exceptional defence against gunfire, improvised explosive devices (IEDs), and underbody mine blasts. To further guarantee mobility during an ambush, the wheels are fitted with a run-flat tyre system, allowing the vehicle to keep driving to safety even if the tyres are shot out or punctured. Beyond its thick armour, the ATT functions as a highly advanced tactical asset. Troops inside can return fire safely from a 360-degree rotating gun turret mounted on the roof. Soldiers also maintain excellent situational awareness through external Pan-Tilt-Zoom (PTZ) surveillance cameras, which monitor the vehicle's surroundings in real-time without exposing the crew. Additionally, a powerful, heavy-duty climate control system ensures the cabin remains comfortable across India's extreme weather conditions and tough terrains. This transporter is also highly versatile. Its modular layout allows it to function not just as a troop carrier, but as a fully integrated mobile command-and-control centre capable of networking with combat drones and unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs) on the battlefield. Serving as a proud milestone for the 'Make in India' initiative, this new fleet of armoured 4x4 transporters ensures that the ultimate sacrifice made by the Pulwama martyrs translates into a safer, highly protected future for India's frontline defenders.
